title: What Belongs Above the Fold on a Small Business Website

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a folded paper website showing five clearly prioritized interface elements.

figures.title: Five questions the first screen should answer
figures.summary: Give a new visitor enough context to choose a next step.

items.label: What?
items.detail: State the specific service or product.

items.label: Who?
items.detail: Name the customers the offer serves.

items.label: Cost?
items.detail: Provide relevant pricing context or estimate information.

figures.caption: The article's five-part content framework. The final arrangement depends on the screen and business.

figures.title: Check the hierarchy on a real phone
figures.summary: Small screens reveal which elements deserve priority.

items.label: Headline first
items.detail: Keep the service and audience understandable without relying on an image.

items.label: Compact context
items.detail: Group service area and pricing context beneath the headline.

items.label: One clear action
items.detail: Make the intended next step prominent and easy to tap.

items.label: Useful imagery
items.detail: Use a compressed image that supports the offer instead of pushing it out of view.

items.label: Device check
items.detail: Review the first screen and scrolling behavior on an actual phone.

figures.caption: A mobile review checklist from the article; the fold varies with device, browser, and text settings.
